Understanding Output P-Values and Result Columns

Source: vignettes/understanding-output-p-values.Rmd
understanding-output-p-values.Rmd

All tests attach columns to pleio@results, with one row per variant. Smaller values usually mean stronger evidence, but not every column has the same null hypothesis or interpretation.

Row Meaning

Rows follow the simulated truth labels produced by run_pleiosim():

  • pleio_variant*: variants that load on all phenotypes in the effect template;
  • nonpleio_variant*: variants that load on exactly one phenotype;
  • null_variant*: variants with no template effect.

Multiple-Association Columns

The MPAT/MTAR columns, tates, and metacca ask whether a variant is associated with any phenotype. Their usual global null is no association with any trait. These are useful for discovery of multi-phenotype association, not necessarily proof of horizontal pleiotropy.

Pleiotropy-Specific Columns

placo, pgctest, and polarmorphism report p-values for pleiotropy-focused hypotheses. placo, pgctest, maiup, and conjfdr are pairwise for the selected i, j traits. polarmorphism is joint across all phenotypes.

Important distinctions:

  • maiup is an empirical FDR-style output based on a mixture-adjusted intersection-union statistic.
  • conjfdr is a conjunctional conditional-FDR-style quantity, not an ordinary p-value.
  • polarmorphism returns NA for variants that do not pass its radial q-value screen.
  • run_acat() creates an ACAT p-value from selected existing result columns.

Pairwise Column Caveat

A pairwise method overwrites or populates a single column name such as placo. If you need every pair, store each result under a separate object or copy the column to a pair-specific name before running the next pair.

pleio <- run_placo(pleio, i = 1, j = 2)
pleio@results$placo_1_2 <- pleio@results$placo
pleio <- run_placo(pleio, i = 1, j = 3)
pleio@results$placo_1_3 <- pleio@results$placo

Practical Sorting 

result_table <- pleio@results
head(result_table[order(result_table$wald), 'wald', drop = FALSE])

Use method-specific thresholds and downstream multiple-testing correction appropriate to your design. The package computes per-variant method outputs; it does not globally adjust all result columns for the full number of variants and methods.
